question: For how many positive integers \(x\) is \(\log_{10}(x - 40)\) \(+ \log_{10}(60 - x) \lt 2?\)
solution:
Both logarithm arguments must be positive, so
\[
x-40>0,\qquad 60-x>0,
\]
and hence \(40<x<60\). On this domain, combine the logarithms. Since the base \(10\) logarithm is increasing and \(2=\log_{10}100\), the given inequality is equivalent to
\[
(x-40)(60-x)<100.
\]
The two factors are equally far from \(10\). Setting \(y=x-50\) reveals a difference of squares:
\[
(x-40)(60-x)=(10+y)(10-y)=100-y^2.
\]
Thus the inequality holds exactly when \(y^2>0\), or \(x\ne50\).

The integers in the domain are \(41,42,\ldots,59\), a total of \(59-41+1=19\). Removing \(50\), where equality holds, leaves \(\boxed{18}\) solutions, choice B.
